content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"The Ballistic Missile Defense Midcourse Defense Segment (program element 0603882C) is run by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) and funds the Ground-Based Midcourse Defense (GMD) Weapon System, which gives combatant commands including U.S. Northern Command (USNORTHCOM) a continuously available homeland-defense system that operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year.","citation":{"fact_id":"3a342a9d49406a23"}},{"text":"The system's Ground Based Interceptors deliver a single kill vehicle to counter threats in space during the midcourse phase of a ballistic missile's flight, and the program is developing a future mixed fleet of Ground Based Interceptors and Next Generation Interceptors.","citation":{"fact_id":"3a342a9d49406a23"}},{"text":"The Ground Systems include the Ground Fire Control (GFC), with two nodes at Fort Greely, Alaska and the Missile Defense Integration and Operations Center in Colorado Springs, Colorado; the communications network; In-flight Data Terminals; and Ground Support Systems located at Fort Greely and Vandenberg Space Force Base, California.","citation":{"fact_id":"ef19558dbef9d485"}},{"text":"The GMD Cyber Operations project provides cybersecurity and cyber resiliency to maintain and operate all mission and mission-support systems, hardening the system against cyber-attacks and reducing vulnerabilities before fielding.","citation":{"fact_id":"017cda8d83a2be1d"}},{"text":"Beginning in FY 2026, MDA is transferring the Ground Based Interceptor and Ground Based Interceptor Service Life Extension Program budget accomplishments into a new accomplishment called Interceptor Fleet Management, yielding a net decrease from efficiencies gained through the fleet-management approach.","citation":{"fact_id":"e89f0a8d93ce2d69"}},{"text":"MDA completed the transition from The Boeing Company as the Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Program Lead System Integrator to MDA itself executing as the Weapon System Integrator.","citation":{"fact_id":"d54c7f771b0f79c9"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"A January 27, 2025 Presidential Executive Order established a goal of protecting U.S. citizens, safeguarding critical infrastructure, and securing second-strike capability against missile attack, and this budget submission reflects changes needed to meet that mission.","citation":{"fact_id":"3a342a9d49406a23"}},{"text":"The program funds interceptor fleet management aimed at sustaining a minimal workforce and infrastructure, maintaining the existing fleet, extending the service life of the Ground Based Interceptors, and executing repairs until they are retired or replaced by Next Generation Interceptors.","citation":{"fact_id":"851e042b32edf007"}},{"text":"The program's actual spending was about $866.6 million (USD thousands: 866,585) in fiscal year 2024.","citation":{"fact_id":"6113ddf090007e3b"}},{"text":"Congress enacted about $752.0 million (751,963 in USD thousands) for fiscal year 2025.","citation":{"fact_id":"1403a74c0e06959d"}},{"text":"The fiscal year 2026 request is about $825.9 million (825,919 in USD thousands).","citation":{"fact_id":"5be35c38f5e46a3e"}},{"text":"The fiscal year 2026 request is about $74.0 million higher than the 2025 total, an increase of roughly 9.84 percent.","citation":{"fact_id":"f0ddc60755455c11"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The largest project within the program is Ground Based Midcourse (project MD08), with a fiscal year 2026 request of about $767.5 million.","citation":{"fact_id":"bf24144a210174a1"}},{"text":"Ground Based Midcourse (project MD08) had actual spending of about $805.5 million in fiscal year 2024.","citation":{"fact_id":"2ae597aa10272cc1"}},{"text":"The Cyber Operations project (MC08) has a fiscal year 2026 request of about $30.3 million.","citation":{"fact_id":"cdc4d5a1a345c316"}},{"text":"The Program-Wide Support project (MD40) has a fiscal year 2026 request of about $28.1 million.","citation":{"fact_id":"1f62a61a92c5a687"}},{"text":"Cumulative prior-year funding for the Ground Based Midcourse project (MD08) totals about $9.2 billion.","citation":{"fact_id":"6249d9d91dcae5ec"}},{"text":"MDA completed the transition from The Boeing Company, which had served as the Lead System Integrator, and awarded contracts including a GWS Contract for Ground Systems and Fire Control and a System Integration, Test, & Readiness (SITR) Contract for Element Engineering.","citation":{"fact_id":"d54c7f771b0f79c9"}},{"text":"Lobbying filings by client BAE Systems Inc referenced the program in a 2026 filing addressing the National Defense Authorization Act, 2027 and provisions on research and development.","citation":{"fact_id":"01f9b661cd76819d"}},{"text":"An earlier 2024 lobbying filing by BAE Systems Inc referenced the program in connection with the Department of Defense Appropriations Act of 2024.","citation":{"fact_id":"004fd92e0be59371"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
